title: beliefs about medicines
guidance: Score what the medication has actually done to this person's conduct, not the strength of what they said about it. A belief that has changed nothing sits lower than one that has changed a dose, a routine, or a decision.
rules: The two specific sub-scales are about their own prescribed medication. A patient with no prescription has no specific belief to hold: score both null, not a middle value.
The two general sub-scales are about medicines as a class, and rarely come up unasked. If you never raised them, they are null, not 3.
A concern that has produced no behaviour is a lower score than one that has.

specific_necessity.label: that their own medication is needed
anchors: Takes it, but doubts they would be much worse off without it.
Accepts it is needed without much conviction either way.
Treats it as important and organises around it: routines, travel, supplies.
Non-negotiable. Stopping is not something they would consider.
specific_necessity.note: Adherence is evidence but not proof. Someone can take a medicine faithfully while doubting it is necessary, and say so.

specific_concerns.label: worries about their own medication
anchors: Raises no concerns, prompted or unprompted.
Concerns only when asked, and nothing has been done about them.
Concerns recur unprompted; they have raised them, or thought about reducing the dose.
Concerns have changed their behaviour: doses altered, delayed, or stopped.
specific_concerns.note: Side effects experienced are not concerns held. What counts is worry about what the drug is doing to them, not the symptom itself.

general_harm.label: that medicines as a class are harmful
anchors: No general view; judges each medicine on its own terms.
Mild generalised caution about taking things long-term.
Holds that medicines generally do harm alongside good, and is wary of them as a group.
Avoids medicines as a class, and prefers alternatives to them.
general_harm.note: This is about medicines in general, not theirs. A patient can be devoted to their own treatment and still hold that medicines as a class are overused and harmful.

general_overuse.label: that doctors prescribe too readily
anchors: No view offered; takes prescribing decisions as given.
Occasional doubt about one particular prescription.
Holds that doctors reach for medication too quickly, as a general pattern.
Distrusts prescribing as a practice, and treats any new prescription with suspicion.
general_overuse.note: Directed at prescribing as a practice, not at their own clinician. Frustration with one doctor is not this belief.
